source.original_question:
In the figure above, the smaller circles are tangent to the larger circle at points A and C, and are tangent to each other at point B. What is the perimeter of the shaded region?
Choices:
A.6*\pi
B.8*\pi
C.9*\pi
D.12*\pi
E.15*\pi

adaptation.reason: The source does not explicitly state the small circles are congruent; added that condition to make the given radius 3 determine both circles. Preserved all original tangencies, shaded boundary, and dashed/nonboundary arcs. The copied renderer has a narrowly scoped native circular-arc fill extension that obeys the same protocol style; no source raster is read.

audit.independent_solution: Both small radii are 3, so each diameter is 6 and the large diameter is 12, giving large radius 6. The shaded boundary consists of one large semicircle and one semicircle from each small circle. Its length is 6π+3π+3π=12π, option D. Dashed small-circle halves are not part of the shaded boundary.
